::: {.chapter-lead}
This path builds a small decoder-only GPT, module by module: a named, validated configuration; numerical building blocks; a Transformer block; the assembled model; then the generation loop. The reference code is tested and lives in [`src/llm_lab/foundations/`](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/tree/main/src/llm_lab/foundations); each module is explained line by line in a guided tour. No prior mastery of linear algebra, tensor calculus or differential calculus is required: notions are introduced when they become useful, with a link to the concept page that explains them.
:::

::: {.callout-note .learning-outcomes collapse="true" title="Learning outcomes"}
By the end of this path, you will be able to:
- place the five modules of the reference code and their order of construction;
- run the reference code and its tests, then verify each available milestone's observable result (tensor shapes, causality, generation loop);
- explain why a randomly initialized GPT produces incoherent text while its mechanics work.
:::

## The code, in construction order

Each module depends only on the previous ones; each can be read and tested on its own.

1. **[The configuration](gpt-config-walkthrough.qmd)** ([`gpt_config.py`](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/src/llm_lab/foundations/gpt_config.py)): name and validate the model's dimensions before any computation.
2. **[The numerical building blocks](gpt-ops-walkthrough.qmd)** ([`gpt_ops.py`](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/src/llm_lab/foundations/gpt_ops.py)): initialization, linear projection, layer normalization, GELU.
3. **[The Transformer block](transformer-block-walkthrough.qmd)** ([`transformer_block.py`](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/src/llm_lab/foundations/transformer_block.py)): multi-head causal attention, MLP and residuals, in pre-LN order.
4. **[Model assembly](gpt-model-walkthrough.qmd)** ([`gpt.py`](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/src/llm_lab/foundations/gpt.py)): embeddings, stacked blocks, projection to logits.
5. **[Generation](gpt-generation-walkthrough.qmd)** ([`generate.py`](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/src/llm_lab/foundations/generate.py)): the autoregressive loop — pick a token, append it to the context, repeat.

## The model, assembled

The whole model fits in a few lines[^exec] — its output is incoherent, and that is expected (see "Generate first, train later"):

```python
config = GPTConfig(
    vocab_size=50,       # V: embedding-table rows, logits per position
    context_length=32,   # T: positions processed in one pass
    embedding_dim=32,    # d: residual-stream width, divisible by num_heads
    num_heads=4,         # H: attention heads
    num_layers=2,        # stacked blocks
    mlp_hidden_dim=64,   # MLP hidden width
    seed=0,              # same seed, same parameters
)
model = GPT(config)
model.num_parameters()  # check against the expected count (milestone 4)

ids = generate(model, np.array([1, 2, 3]), max_new_tokens=8)  # greedy decoding
ids = generate(model, np.array([1, 2, 3]), max_new_tokens=8, greedy=False,
               temperature=0.8, rng=np.random.default_rng(42))  # sampling
```

The reference code is pure NumPy (float64): readability first, speed later.

## Understand, build, deepen

At each milestone:

- **Understand** the mechanism: the linked concept page explains it — consult it when the question arises rather than beforehand.
- **Build** the corresponding operation and check the observed result.
- **Deepen** only as needed: reading a tensor shape is enough to debug an operation; understanding what a gradient represents is enough to train. [Tensors](tensors.qmd) and the [mathematical chain of training](mathematical-foundations.qmd) serve as reference when the need arises.

## Generate first, train later

The same model computation serves two distinct uses: **generate** a token with fixed parameters, or **learn** by comparing predictions with targets and then updating the parameters. The panorama details this [distinction between learning and inference](llm-overview.qmd).

The path builds the generation path first. A **randomly initialized** GPT produces incoherent text — an expected result, not a bug: the shapes, the causal mask and the loop all work; only the quality acquired through learning is missing. This separation motivates the learning milestones: preparing [training examples](training-examples.qmd), optimizing a [loss](loss.qmd) with [gradients](gradients.qmd) — of which only the loss computations exist today (`losses.py`). The generation loop itself is detailed in [Generating text: inference step by step](generation.qmd).

## Build milestones

Before moving to the next step, produce or verify the indicated result; concept pages supply the mechanism, not proof that the code exists. The **G0–G9** identifiers are those of the [versioned build plan](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/learning-path.md); **G2** (training data) is a parallel branch: required before training, not for generation.

| Step | What you build | Result to verify | To understand | Code status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 · G0. Define the model | The scope: a decoder-only GPT predicting the next token | Place this model among LLM families and Transformer architectures | [LLM panorama](llm-overview.qmd), [GPT and Transformer](transformer.qmd), [history](transformer-history.qmd) as context | Conceptual |
| 1 · G1. Prepare text input | Encoding and decoding a prompt with the tokenizer | Encode then decode a short text; identify the effect of special tokens and tokenizer version | [Text and data](text-data.qmd), [Unicode](unicode-text.qmd), [tokenization](tokenization-strategies.qmd) | Conceptual — no validated tokenizer pipeline |
| 2 · G3. Represent tokens | Embedding lookup and positional information | Trace shapes from `[B, L]` to `[B, L, D]` and name each axis | [Embedding space](embedding-space.qmd), [position](positional-encoding.qmd) | Reference — inside `gpt.py`; [tour: model](gpt-model-walkthrough.qmd) |
| 3 · G4. Compute attention | Q/K/V projections, scores, softmax and causal mask | In evaluation mode, change a future token without altering earlier-position outputs | [Q/K/V](queries-keys-values.qmd), [attention](scaled-dot-product-attention.qmd), [causal masking](causal-masking.qmd) | Reference — `attention.py` (`scaled_dot_product_attention`, `causal_mask`, `softmax_with_temperature`); [tour: block](transformer-block-walkthrough.qmd) |
| 4 · G5. Assemble the GPT | Stacking the blocks: residuals, normalization, MLP and output projection | Trace dimensions through the model and check the parameter count (`model.num_parameters()`) | [Transformer](transformer.qmd), [tensors](tensors.qmd) as reference | Reference — [tours: block](transformer-block-walkthrough.qmd) and [model](gpt-model-walkthrough.qmd) |
| 5 · G6. Predict and select | Turning logits into a distribution, then the decoding rule | Distinguish logits from probabilities; explain greedy or sampled selection | [Logits](logits.qmd), [probabilities](probabilities.qmd), [generation step by step](generation.qmd) | Reference — inside `generate.py`; [tour: generation](gpt-generation-walkthrough.qmd) |
| 6 · G7. Generate before training | The full autoregressive loop, with random parameters | Run the loop: incoherent output expected, stopping and context window checked | [Generation step by step](generation.qmd) | Reference — [tour: generation](gpt-generation-walkthrough.qmd) |
| 7 · G2. Prepare training data | A documented, partitioned corpus; input windows, shifted targets, batches and masks — a parallel branch of the learning path | Build a window and its shifted target; test boundaries, padding and split hygiene | [Text and data](text-data.qmd), [training examples](training-examples.qmd) | Conceptual — pipeline to be built |
| 8 · G8. Train and validate | Loss, backpropagation, optimizer, validation and checkpoints | Align logits and targets, compute the loss, reproduce a small update, track training and validation losses separately | [Cross-entropy](cross-entropy.qmd), [loss](loss.qmd), [gradients](gradients.qmd) | Partial — `losses.py` (`cross_entropy_from_logits`, `cross_entropy_gradient`); full loop to be built |
| 9 · G9 / E1. Evaluate | Baselines, metrics, error analysis and limits | Compare against a baseline under an explicit protocol; state what the metrics do not establish | [Experimental evaluation](experimental-evaluation.qmd) | Method available — no complete evaluation of a trained GPT |

These criteria are learning objectives: an available page, a hand-checkable example, an automated test and a reproducible run are different levels of evidence.

## To continue

- [Exercises and practice](exercises.qmd): apply the milestones to exercises, separately from conceptual questions.
- [Versioned build plan](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/learning-path.md): prerequisites, expected evidence, dependencies and validation criteria for each milestone.

[^exec]: Nothing to install beyond Python 3.12+ and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/): clone the repository (`git clone https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab.git` then `cd llm-lab`), sync the environment with `uv sync --dev`, and run the tests with `uv run pytest`. The snippet on the page assumes `import numpy as np` then `from llm_lab.foundations import GPT, GPTConfig, generate`. Every module has its test file, in reading order: `test_gpt_config.py`, `test_gpt_ops.py`, `test_transformer_block.py`, `test_gpt.py` and `test_generate.py` follow the five modules; `test_attention.py` and `test_losses.py` cover the attention and loss primitives.

::: {.callout-warning}
**An educational project, not industrial-scale training.** The small randomly initialized GPT makes transformations and errors inspectable; it does not reproduce the data volumes, compute resources or performance of a production LLM.
:::
